MUQATIL:68:17-27/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r6.claim: They set out whispering among themselves.

MAJAZ:v2p265/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p265/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p265/r2.claim: Yatakhāfatūn means they whisper to one another.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.claim: They whispered to one another not to let a poor person enter the garden that day.

NAHHAS:v5p11/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p11/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p11/r1.claim: The clause describing their departure is circumstantial.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r6.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r6.claim: يتخافتون can mean that they were talking.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r7.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r7.claim: يتخافتون can mean whispering and concealing their speech so nobody would know of their plan.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r8.claim: يتخافتون may mean hiding themselves from people so they would not see them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r9.claim: يتخافتون may mean that they did not consult one another.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r5.claim: فانطلقوا means they went to their garden, whispering among themselves that no poor person should enter that day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they went at dusk, whispering so that no poor person would find out.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r7.claim: Qatada says their charitable father kept enough for himself and gave away the surplus; after his death his sons stopped the charity and resolved to bar the poor.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r2.claim: They set out while whispering secretly among themselves.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.claim: They set out whispering privately to one another that no poor person should enter the garden that day.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r4.claim: يتخافتون means speaking quietly; they whisper because they fear the poor will notice, saying not to let a poor person enter.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r7.claim: They went off speaking in whispers; the verb comes from the sense of making oneself quiet or hidden.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#5/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#5/r1.claim: They went to their garden whispering secretly to one another.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r1.claim: Takhaffut means speaking secretly; khafiya, khafata, and khafada all mean concealment, and khafadūd is a bat.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they went early, whispering to each other so that no poor person would learn of their plan.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r6.claim: The sons called one another at daybreak to set out and harvest; the verb means that one person called another.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r7.claim: Qatada explains “your harvest” as the crop they planned to reap.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r8.claim: Mujahid says their harvest was grapes, and they did not say “if God wills.”

QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.claim: Ata and Qatada say the brothers whispered and concealed their speech so no one would learn of their plan.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.claim: The verb may mean they hid themselves from people, since their father used to alert the poor to come at harvest time.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r3.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:23-25/r3.claim: Duraid ibn al-Simma’s verse is cited as evidence for the word khufatan, a quiet or secret manner.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r1.claim: They whispered and conferred secretly; خفى, خفت, and خفد share that meaning, and خفدود names a bat.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#3/r1.claim: They went off whispering to one another so the poor would not hear.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.claim: They whispered so the poor would not hear them; their secret plan was to keep anyone poor from entering the garden.

SAMIN-DURR:68:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:23/r1.claim: وهم يتخافتون is a circumstantial clause describing those who set out.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.claim: They spoke secretly so no one could hear their plan to prevent a poor person from entering the garden that day.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r4.claim: They set out promptly and whispered like people planning a theft; takhafut derives from quietness or stillness.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were whispering and speaking quietly.

BURSEVI:v10p88/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88/r3.claim: They set out toward the garden and whispered secretly so nobody would hear and interfere.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r1.claim: They set out while consulting one another in whispers; خفي, خفت, and خفد all convey concealment.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31/r2.claim: The related words include الخفدود for a bat and الخفود for a she-camel that drops her fetus before it has developed.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.claim: They forgot that the previous day they had needed oaths to reassure each other and establish their company; the orchard's yield would likewise depend on trust.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.claim: They rushed out without considering the orchard's condition and whispered their exclusion of the poor so no one would hear.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r10.claim: التخافت is the reciprocal form of خفت, speaking quietly.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.claim: They went quietly, consulting in secret to keep poor people from noticing and claiming a share of the harvested fruit.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.claim: Takhāfut means whispering to one another so no one else hears the plan.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.claim: The brothers’ exclusion of the poor violated an ancient Near Eastern custom allowing the poor to glean and the Quranic command to give the harvest due on harvest day.
